agents.angle: mechanics/correctness attack: executable identity, hashing, restart, atomicity, failure boundaries, test adequacy, and actual descriptor coverage
agents.initial_prompt: Read every path in target_bindings from docs/features/agents-communication-infra/reviews/2026-07-25-host-bus-phase-a-close/proposal-v1.json and verify its SHA-256 before analysis. Attack the entire corpus through mechanics/correctness only: executable identity continuity from parent dispatch through host binding, reveal and materialized input; exact bytes and hashes; restart/idempotency; atomic rollback; migration/service wiring; focused-test adequacy; descriptor/readiness write-scope and prerequisite coverage; source-manifest correspondence. You may run non-mutating focused tests. Return candidate findings only when you can quote the exact artifact, assign CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR, name a one-line fix, and state the check that verifies it. Also state what you attacked when no finding survives. Do not mutate files or use network.

agents.angle: fidelity/governance attack: authority ownership, schema compatibility, claim-proof alignment, source integrity, forbidden effects, and spec-to-runtime correspondence
agents.initial_prompt: Read every path in target_bindings from docs/features/agents-communication-infra/reviews/2026-07-25-host-bus-phase-a-close/proposal-v1.json and verify its SHA-256 before analysis. groups.predicted_disagreement: Lamport runs the mechanics/correctness attack and Liskov runs the fidelity/governance attack on the attack-vector axis. Lamport may accept a governance description that follows working mechanics, while Liskov may reject a passing implementation whose receipts or semantics overclaim; a mechanics-only bias internal to Lamport is exposed by Liskov's governance contradictions, while a document-fidelity bias internal to Liskov is exposed by Lamport's executable counterexamples.
